component.name: Familiar
component.summary: Play MUDs, MUSHes, MUCKs and MOOs

description.p: Familiar is a client for text-based multiplayer worlds: MUDs, MUSHes, MUCKs and MOOs. It is inspired by BeipMU and can import BeipMU's settings, maps and scripts.

ul.li: Tabs for each world, colour and Unicode output, clickable links and logging
Triggers, aliases, keyboard macros, variables and JavaScript scripting
A map that draws itself from GMCP Room.Info, and walks you to any room
GMCP stat bars, server sounds, web views and inline images
MCP 2.1 with a program editor that highlights and indents MOO and MUF code
Puppets in their own tabs, text to speech and spell checking
A terminal version with the same features, for SSH and tiling setups

description.p: A native app for Windows, and examples to learn triggers, aliases and macros from.

ul.li: On Windows, Familiar is now an app written for Windows 11, with web views, spell checking in every language Windows has, and find in the output
The triggers, aliases and macros editor can add a set of examples, each showing one thing the rules can do; triggers and aliases arrive switched off
In the terminal client, /editor syntax installs MOO highlighting for micro, Emacs, Vim and Neovim

description.p: Bouncer support, and fixes to selecting text in the terminal client.

ul.li: Worlds can connect through an mbnc bouncer, which keeps your character online while you're away and replays what arrived when you return
In the terminal client, holding a mouse selection at the top or bottom edge of the output scrolls it, so the selection can go on
In the terminal client, selecting downwards while scrolled back no longer jumps into the live lines

description.p: Familiar now runs on macOS, and the terminal client can show your editor beside the world.

ul.li: The terminal client can open your editor beside the world, where the sidebar goes, when the sidebar is free (/editor sidebar). F6 switches between the two and F7 moves the editor to a tab and back
A native app for macOS, and the terminal client for macOS

description.p: Three additions to the terminal client.

ul.li: Your editor opens in a tab of its own, so the world stays in view while you edit
A window for triggers, aliases, keyboard macros and variables (F2)
Drag over the output to select text; it is copied when you let go

description.p: Familiar now runs on Windows as well as Linux.

ul.li: A Preferences dialog, with font selection; worlds can have their own font
The terminal client draws the 16 basic colours exactly, whatever the terminal's theme
The first lines of a session are no longer hidden above the top of the output
Addresses can be IPv6 and can end in "tls"
